body: I would suggest a check if the column type is `BIT(1)` then return `true` for `0x01` and `false` for `0x00`.

Im not a yii2 developer or maintainer.

But just did some sort of testing your issue.

Here is my gist of test: https://gist.github.com/d89b4e325f29bc0b3371

When `asArray` approach imply that there wont be done any type casting
by framework. And pure output from PDO will be returned as result.

PDO result of bit(1) column with b'0' value is string "0" and for
column with b'1' - string "1". You can prove it by invoking this pure
php script. https://gist.github.com/c735596977d1ecadf2c6

So it's what PDO returns. And when you compare strings "0" and "1"
with ascii characters `NUL` and `SOH` by executing something like
this:

```
php -r 'var_dump("1"===chr(0x01), "0"===chr(0x00));'
```

You will always get false. Because hex ascii code for string "1" is
0x31 and for string "0" is 0x30.

Can be closed.

Have not seen you tried to do just `find()->all()`.

My test 

``` php
$r = MyModel::find()->all();
var_dump(r);
```

first model `test` attribute equals to false. 
and second - equals to true. 

master branch yiisoft/yii2 repository

You can see that `test` is returned as `boolean` and not as string! `true` both time, no matter that I have just b'0' and b'1' in the database, so there is an issue for sure. My table structure is in the first post.

The framework **does** type cast from string to bool, and sees b'0' and b'1' as `true` which is absolutely wrong. I'm developing an application that uses a lot of `bit(1)` columns, and the fix I use at the moment is fetching `asArray` and compare like `$result['test'] === chr(0x00)` and `$result['test'] === chr(0x01)` and it is working, so `asArray` do **not** return string, but the `0x00` and `0x01` chars.

I have found and fixed the issue with pull request #9205 . 0x01 and 0x31 (string '1') are considered as true, otherwise false. It seems the issue is in PHP's (bool) cast function.

Suppose that it's not Yii issue. And something specific in your
environment. Because on my side everything is OK.

@RusAlex Probably you can't reproduce the issue because you're using MariaDB which has differences compared with MySQL, or it is the PHP (PDO) version. Using MySQL 5.5.44 with PHP 5.6.9 and the latest yii2 framework the raw data received from a `BIT(1)` column is definetly not `0x30` or `0x31`, but `0x00` and `0x01`.

Anyhow, php's `bool` seems to be broken:
`php -r 'var_dump((bool) chr(0x00));'` returns `true` as well as `php -r 'var_dump((bool) chr(0x01));'`
I have reported this to PHP's team, as I cannot see any valid reason why 0x00 is considered as true, but also I believe the pull request wont hurt, as it does not break BC and the bug fix will be delivered to all yii users much faster than waiting for PHP update.
